newsitem.title: USA: Arden sees FY97 EPS of $0.27-$0.29.
newsitem.headline: Arden sees FY97 EPS of $0.27-$0.29.

text.p: Arden Industrial Products Inc chief executive officer Larry Carlson said Monday he expects the company's earnings per share for the fiscal year 1997 to be between $0.27 and $0.29.

"The estimates are for between $0.27 to $0.29 per share for fiscal year 1997. We're comfortable with the estimates. We think we're going to get there. Personally, I'm more optimistic, but that's where we think we'll be," Carlson told Reuters after the company's annual meeting.
For the fiscal year ended June 30, 1996, the fasteners distributor reported earnings of $0.06 per share.
Carlson told Reuters the company would be dividing its sales force into two groups targeting different customer segments.

"Our sales people used to sell to both inventory managements accounts and to traditional business. Now a focused group is going to sell to the inventory management side and another sales force to the traditional accounts," he said.

The inventory management accounts represent larger original equipment manufacturers (OEM) who are interested in the company's just-in-time inventory management service. The traditional accounts consist of smaller OEMs.

Carlson said he anticipated a slight improvement in the company's gross margin. "We think our gross margin will kick up and see some slight improvement (in FY97). We're counting on our new information system to help us buy better and reduce our inventory obsolescence problem," he said. "We're doing a much better job of product sourcing. We're importing more product for those customers who desire that."

Arden has been plagued with costs associated with the conversion of its operating software and Carlson told shareholders those problems persist. "We're working diligently to get the bugs fixed in our information system," he said.
Arden's chief financial officer, Kim Erickson, told shareholders he expected to incur costs associated with the information systems conversion through the fiscal year's second quarter.

"We still have a period during which we'll be stabilizing the day-to-day implementation. We're still incurring additional costs from the consulting perspective, we and see that going on through the fiscal year's second quarter," Erickson added.
